title: Kitchen and Vow
premise: Isandro Coldharbour, a pastry chef drowning in debt, agrees to pose as the fiancée of vineyard heir Theo Marchetti at his family's reunion in exchange for a loan that could save her café. What begins as a transaction deepens into real love, but Theo's mother Camille wields the family fortune like a weapon, demanding Isandro sign away her café and her name to be deemed worthy. When Isandro discovers the 'loan' was a trap designed to make her dependent, she must choose between the security she's never had and the man who let her believe in it. In the end, Isandro speaks the vow she rehearsed for a decade — not at an altar, but standing on her own terms — and Theo, finally defying his mother, chooses her over the inheritance.
about_author: Beatrix Pemberton is a former restaurant critic who spent ten years writing about other people's love stories before daring to write her own. She lives above a bakery in coastal Maine, where she insists all first drafts must be written within smell of fresh bread.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The bank calls during the morning rush; her café is ninety days from foreclosure. A mysterious offer arrives: Theo Marchetti needs a fake fiancée for his family reunion, and he'll pay enough to save everything. Beat: desperation dressed up as opportunity.

chapters.title: The Contract with a Dessert Clause
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She meets Theo to negotiate terms — strict rules, no feelings, one weekend extended indefinitely by a meddling grandmother. He reveals the reunion is really a succession trial for control of the vineyard empire. Beat: wary alliance sealed over burnt caramel.

chapters.title: Arrival at Vespera Vineyard
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They arrive at the estate, and Theo watches Isandro charm his hostile relatives effortlessly while he fumbles the performance he scripted. His mother Camille sizes Isandro up like a threat assessment. Beat: the fake begins working too well.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Decade
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Grandmother Lucia pulls Isandro aside and mentions a vow Theo has rehearsed since childhood — words he's never said aloud. Isandro realizes the engagement story has layers she wasn't told. Beat: curiosity curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On the eve of first harvest, Theo and Isandro share a stolen night in the barrel room; the fake date becomes real by dessert. But Camille photographs them together and makes her first move. Beat: surrender, shadowed by surveillance.

chapters.title: The Mother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Camille offers Isandro a deal: sign over her café as 'collateral' and become a proper Marchetti, or lose Theo and the loan simultaneously. Isandro sees the trap — dependence disguised as generosity. Beat: power shows its teeth.

chapters.title: What the Vineyard Owes
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers his mother engineered Isandro's original financial ruin to manufacture this exact leverage. Confronted, Camille argues love is just another acquisition. Theo wavers between dynasty and heart. Beat: the corruption revealed.

chapters.title: The Sentence Unsaid
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Feeling betrayed that Theo hid the truth of her sabotage, Isandro walks out mid-harvest festival, leaving him publicly humiliated before the family. She returns to a café with a final notice taped to the door. Beat: lowest point; love against duty breaks.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On harvest day, Theo publicly renounces his claim to the vineyard, exposing Camille's ledger to the board, while Isandro fights to keep her café through means of her own making. Their separate battles converge at her doorstep. Beat: both choose integrity over safety.

chapters.title: Kitchen and Vow
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. With nothing contractual left between them, Theo asks for something real. In her flour-dusted kitchen, Isandro finally says the sentence she rehearsed for a decade — not as a Marchetti, but as herself. Epilogue beat: the café reopens; the vineyard gets a new pastry counter; the vow is kept.
